area: Submission attachments, library, review cards, worklist, photo evidence page

Locate a specific submission by ID/district/county/route/post mile and open it
Delete a draft (owner) or any record (admin)

responsive.layout: Vertical stack inside AppShell (sidebar stacks above content below lg): stat grid → filter bar → full-width table in an overflow-x-auto card → footer.
breakpointsUsed: flex-col xl:flex-row xl:items-end for filter bar (L188)
overflow-x-auto + table-fixed + colgroup w-20 w-80 w-36 w-36 w-48 w-48 w-32 = 75rem/1200px fixed table (L219-221)
phoneRisks: Table is a fixed 1200px wide (colgroup L221) inside overflow-x-auto (L219): on a 375px phone the user sees only the ID column and a slice of the descriptor; Status, Submitted and the primary Review action sit ~800px to the right and require horizontal panning.

The ••• dropdown is absolutely positioned inside the overflow-x-auto container (L219,L240); overflow-x:auto forces overflow-y:auto, so a menu opened on the last row is clipped/scrolls inside the table box.
••• button (px-2.5 py-1.5 text-sm, L240) and Review/Open links (py-1.5, L239) are ~32px tall — under a 44px touch target.
Hover-only tooltips carry the raw timestamps and 'Creator user ID' (title attributes L234-236) — unreachable on touch.
Summary cards fall to 2 columns (L169) so the 5th card (Draft) sits alone on a third row.
tabletRisks: 1200px fixed table still overflows at 768–1024px (content width ≈ 680–940px), so the Action column is off-screen on iPad portrait and partly on landscape.

At md (768px) the filter grid needs 260+220+220px + 2×8px gaps = 716px but only ≈680px is available (AppShell px-6 + page p-5), and AppShell's product-card is overflow-hidden (ui/AppShell.tsx:185), so the Sort select is clipped until ≈810px.
desktopNotes: At ≥1280px the filter bar goes single-row with Clear/Refresh on the right (L188).

Table width is capped by the colgroup so on wide screens (max-w-[1900px] shell) the table does not stretch; w-full + table-fixed distributes the 75rem proportionally, leaving the Submission column comfortably wide.

painPoints.issue: Search, status counts and sort operate only on the rows already loaded (50 per page); a reviewer searching for an older ID gets 'No submissions match these filters' until they click Load older repeatedly, and the placeholder promises server-like search.
Fixed 1200px table (colgroup) forces horizontal scrolling on phones and tablets with the primary Review action in the far-right column.
Summary cards read like global KPIs ('Submitted 3 — Awaiting review') but count only the loaded page; nothing in the card says so ('Loaded' card hint aside).
Two controls for the same status filter (summary cards and a select), and the select shows raw enum codes ('REJECTED') while the cards say 'Returned'; the badge also shows the raw code.
Reporter column shows 'User #id' — no name or email, unusable for a coordinator who thinks in people.
••• menu has no outside-click or Escape dismissal and no role=menu semantics, unlike the tile Open menu; it can also be clipped by the table's overflow container.
Filter grid's fixed 220px columns overflow the available width between 768px and ≈810px and get clipped by the overflow-hidden shell card.
Refresh silently discards any older pages the user loaded and resets the open row menu; there is no 'updated at' indicator.

Worklist has no navigation entry and no breadcrumb, yet it is the RoleRoute fallback destination; users bounced here have no highlighted nav item (non-operational) or a misleading 'Assessments' highlight (operational).
Error and loading states are plain divs without role=alert/aria-live or aria-busy, so screen readers are not told the list changed or failed.

strengths: Status summary cards double as the filter with aria-pressed state — one tap to see the review queue (L173-184).
SUBMITTED rows are tinted and get a brand-filled 'Review' CTA while others get a neutral 'Open' — the queue is visually obvious (L230,L239).
Cursor pagination with duplicate-id guard and a footer that states exactly how many rows are loaded (L71-89,L250-253).
Descriptor 'District-County-Route-PM - date' is a far better row identity than a bare id (utils/submissionLabel.ts:33-41).
Distinct empty states for 'nothing accessible' vs 'over-filtered', with an inline Clear filters (L225).
Delete is gated client-side to admin / draft-owner and always confirmed in a modal (L96-101,L256).

responsive.layout: Full-width card: header (title + count left, filter pills right, flex-wrap) → tile grid auto-fill minmax(min(200px,100%),1fr); selecting 'Open here' swaps the grid for a single viewer.
breakpointsUsed: index.css:127-142 hover / focus-within / hover:none rules for the action overlay
phoneRisks: Tiles go single-column at ≈300px wide — fine — but the four filter pills plus counts wrap under the title and the whole header becomes ~3 rows (SubmissionLibrary.tsx:27-58).
Open/Download overlay buttons are text-xs px-2 py-1 (≈24px tall) — well under a 44px touch target (SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:158,273).
Full file name and full section label are exposed only via title tooltips (L126,L281) — unreadable on touch.
PDF preview is an iframe with h-[70vh] and no error fallback (L317); iOS Safari renders only the first page with no scrolling, so 'Open here' on a multi-page PDF is a dead end on phones.
'Open in a new window' uses a popup feature string (L82) which mobile browsers ignore or block.
tabletRisks: Grid yields 3 tiles per row at ≈680px content width; section chips are capped at max-w-[60%] and truncate (L126) so 'Pavement / Ground Status' is cut on 200–220px tiles.
Same iPad PDF-iframe limitation as phones.
Inside the modal variant (see next screen) the grid scrolls in a max-h-[88vh] area.
desktopNotes: Action overlay appears on hover or focus-within (index.css:132-136), so keyboard users can reach Open/Download.
Open menu min-w-48 (192px) pops upward inside a tile whose article and image area are overflow-hidden (L164,L248,L251); at the 200px minimum tile width the menu's right edge is clipped by ~8px.
Viewer content is capped at 70vh so it never pushes the page.

painPoints.issue: Media type is printed three times on every tile (glyph label when no thumbnail, top-left badge, type label under the name) plus an internal '#id' — the tile foot is mostly noise.
PDF 'Open here' uses a bare iframe with no onError/fallback and 70vh height; on iOS/iPadOS it shows a single unscrollable page, and the 'Preview unavailable' fallback is only wired to img/video.
Download silently falls back to opening the file in a new tab when the cross-origin fetch fails, so the user who clicked 'Download' gets an unexpected navigation with no explanation.
Filter pills use role=tablist/role=tab without a tabpanel or arrow-key handling — screen readers announce tabs that do not behave like tabs.
Open menu uses role=menu/menuitem but has no arrow-key navigation or focus move into the menu; Escape/outside-click are handled.
Overlay action buttons (~24px) and filter pills (~26px) are below touch-target minimums; hover-only title tooltips hide the full file name and section label on touch.
Selecting 'Open here' hides the whole grid; there is no next/previous between files, so stepping through 15 photos means 15 round trips via 'Back to files'.

Every photo tile fires its own GET /attachments/{id}/download-url on mount when not seeded from the photo-map; 30 photos = 30 requests before any thumbnail shows, and there is no skeleton state (glyph shows instead).
Library is only reachable by scrolling past the entire GISA canvas and notes; the header's evidence button goes to a different page rather than jumping to the library.

strengths: Section chips translate the mobile form's section_key values into GISA section names, giving reviewers the context the old flat attachments table lacked (submissionAttachmentModel.ts:19-37,74-78).
Media classification by MIME with kind as fallback lives in one pure module with tests (submissionAttachmentModel.ts:80-97).

Presigned URL resolver caches per attachment with an early-refresh TTL and de-duplicates in-flight requests; photo-map URLs seed the cache so thumbnails often need no extra request (SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:16-75).
Action overlay is hover-revealed on pointer devices but permanently visible on hover:none devices and on focus-within — a rare correct handling of hover-only affordances (index.css:127-142).
Busy states ('Opening…', 'Saving…') and a dismissable error banner give feedback for the async URL fetch (L160,L276,L383-388).
Empty-state copy distinguishes 'nothing attached' from 'nothing matches this filter' (SubmissionLibrary.tsx:65).

phoneRisks: Modal becomes ≈343px wide with single-column tiles; scrolling happens inside the body while the page behind is locked — workable.

22px-tall 'Open attachments' button is below any touch-target guidance.

strengths: Contextual evidence: the count badge appears exactly where the reviewer is reading, and the dialog reuses the library tiles with the redundant section chip removed (L8-21,L53).

responsive.layout: SubmissionDetailCardGrid: auto-fit minmax(min(420px,100%),1fr) → 1 column below ≈880px content width, 2 columns to ≈1320px, 3 columns above; each card is a bordered section with uppercase brand title, optional subtitle and actions slot.
breakpointsUsed: flex-wrap headers and rows (SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:51; SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:48; SubmissionAccessSharing.tsx:58,86)
phoneRisks: Summary rows use a fixed 1/3 label column (grid-cols-3, L22): at ≈300px the value column is ≈190px, so raw ISO timestamps like 2026-09-04T18:22:11.123456+00:00 wrap awkwardly.
Workflow event header wraps the timestamp under the label (flex-wrap, SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:48) — fine.
Grant/Revoke rows wrap the button under the name/email (flex-wrap, SubmissionAccessSharing.tsx:58,86); buttons are py-1.5 text-xs (~28px) — small targets.
Reviewer note textarea is w-full 4 rows — fine.
tabletRisks: Single column at 768px portrait (content ≈680px < 2×420px), so Access Sharing sits far below Reviewer Note; at 1024px landscape two columns fit only if the sidebar is collapsed (sidebar w-64 at lg, ui/AppShell.tsx:165).
desktopNotes: Three cards (or four with Access Sharing) sit in 2–3 columns; heights differ (Workflow History grows with events) so the row has ragged bottoms — cards are flex-col but not stretched to a common height content-wise.

painPoints.issue: Summary card values pass through String(value), so Created/Updated/Submitted/Reviewed are raw ISO strings and Status is the raw enum, while every other surface formats dates.
Workflow events print the raw event code ('Event SUBMIT') directly under its human label and identify the actor as 'user #id' — no name.

Reviewer note has no explicit save affordance or unsaved indicator; the only cue that it is persisted with Approve/Return is a subtitle, and a note typed by a reviewer who then navigates away is lost.
Grant and Revoke buttons are visually identical neutral buttons; Revoke (destructive) has no confirmation.
Share search results are silently truncated to 25 with no 'refine your search' message.
Card titles are styled divs, not headings, so the four review cards are invisible to screen-reader heading navigation (the library uses an h2).
Compatibility aliases S, R and Section remain exported; Section accepts an 'open' prop it ignores and S/Section have no importers (only R is used).

strengths: Cards are always open — the previous collapsed <details> sections hid the reviewer note and history (SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:29-33).
Workflow event codes are mapped to plain-language labels ('Returned for correction') and transitions are rendered as 'Draft → Submitted' (submissionReviewerSupportModel.ts:3-25,69-78).
Reviewer note is still readable (disabled textarea with value) for non-reviewers, with a subtitle explaining why it is read-only (SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:24,31).
Access sharing copy is explicit about scope ('without changing ownership or edit permissions') and the search uses type=search with a visible label (SubmissionAccessSharing.tsx:33-45).
Candidates exclude users who already have access and are sorted by name (submissionAccessSharingModel.ts:18-29).

entryPoints: Detail header button labelled '{n} photos · {m} mapped' (or 'Photo evidence' / 'Checking evidence…') (features/submissions/SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:71-75,117-122)
Location hero 'Photo evidence details' link inside the 'Mapped evidence' box (features/submissions/SubmissionLocationHero.tsx:217-222)
exits: Open original leaves to object storage in a new tab (SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:143)
AppShell sidebar; no breadcrumb; the linked incident is text, not a link

responsive.layout: AppShell page: back link → header card → 4 stat cards → context card → photo cards (1 column, 2 at xl), each card = image area on top and a definition list below.
breakpointsUsed: flex-col sm:flex-row for the header card (SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:76)
sm:flex-row for name/Open original row (L141); dl sm:grid-cols-2 (L146); correction grid sm:grid-cols-2 (L158)
phoneRisks: Image well is min-h-72 (288px) with object-contain, so a landscape photo at ≈300px width renders ≈225px tall and letterboxes inside a 288px grey box; portrait photos can reach 544px.
Stat cards are 2×2 (L90) — fine. Definition list is single column below sm so each card is very tall (image + 6 dl items + details).
Evidence-context coordinates use text-right inside a flex-wrap row (L106-115); when it wraps under the incident line it is right-aligned while the label is left-aligned.
'Open original' (py-1.5 text-sm ≈32px) is the only sub-44px control; details/summary is native and touch-friendly.
tabletRisks: Photo grid stays single-column until xl (1280px), so on a 1024px iPad every card is full-width with images up to 544px tall — heavy scrolling for 20+ photos.
Header card goes side-by-side at sm — fine.
desktopNotes: Two-column photo grid from 1280px; 'MIME Type' and 'Altitude' occupy slots that could hold a map thumbnail.
Images load directly from presigned URLs (900 s TTL noted in SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:16); after ~15 minutes idle the tags fail and show 'Preview unavailable' until Refresh.

painPoints.issue: The page is about mapped telemetry but shows no map: coordinates and headings are printed as numbers while the actual photo map with heading wedges lives on the detail page (SubmissionArcGisMap), so the reviewer must flip between pages to relate a photo to its location.

Images and 'Open original' use the raw presigned download_url with no refresh; the URL expires after 900 s so a page left open shows broken previews with a misleading 'Preview unavailable in this browser' message.
Section is shown as the raw key ('Section: highway_status') while the library translates the same key to 'Highway Status'; MIME type and Attachment #id are also exposed.
'Photo evidence' title and purpose sentence are repeated immediately under the H1 'Photo Evidence — …'.
Correction history reports only Yes/No flags and 'user #id'; the override coordinates/heading returned by the API are not displayed, so a reviewer cannot see what was changed.
Linked incident is plain text although /incidents/:id exists; no breadcrumb (Submissions › #id › Photo evidence).

This page largely duplicates the detail page's Submission library (same photos, same URLs) with a different card design, different timestamp format and a second URL strategy — two ways to view the same photos.
Error and loading messages are not announced (no role=status/alert); the Refresh button gives no success feedback.
Wrong/unknown submission ids fail silently for the title (catch → null) and the panel only reports the photo-map error, so a 404 reads as 'Photo Evidence — Submission #999' with an error banner.

strengths: Per-photo Mapped/Unmapped, Heading recorded and Corrected telemetry badges give an immediate trust signal without reading the numbers (L137).
Not-recorded values are spelled out ('Not recorded', 'Not mapped', 'Not usable') instead of blanks or nulls (L15-28,147-152).
Correction history is progressively disclosed in a native <details> element (L155-165).
Summary cards separate 'Mapped' from 'With Heading', matching how the header button summarises evidence quality (L90-103; SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:71-75).
Non-image MIME types get an explicit fallback instead of a broken image (L128,134-135).

crossCutting: Vocabulary — status: 'Returned' (worklist card SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:160; workflow label submissionReviewerSupportModel.ts:8) vs raw 'REJECTED' in the status badge (SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:15), the status select (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:198), the delete dialog (SubmissionDeleteDialog.tsx:45) and the Summary card (pages/SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:1298).

Vocabulary — people: the same field is 'Reporter' (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:222), 'Creator' (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:234; SubmissionDeleteDialog.tsx:46), 'owner' (SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:105) and 'Actor user' (SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:52); every one of them is rendered as a numeric 'User #id' because the API exposes only ids.

Vocabulary — files: 'Submission library' (SubmissionLibrary.tsx:33), 'attachments' (SubmissionSectionAttachmentsDialog.tsx:18,45), 'files' (SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:327; submissionAttachmentModel.ts:137), 'items' (submissionAttachmentModel.ts:138), 'Photo evidence' / 'Mapped evidence' (SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:78; SubmissionLocationHero.tsx:219), and title-case 'Photo Evidence' vs sentence-case 'Photo evidence' on the same page (pages/SubmissionPhotoEvidencePage.tsx:35-37 vs SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:78).

Section names: the library maps section_key to GISA titles ('Highway Status', submissionAttachmentModel.ts:19-37) but the photo evidence page prints the raw key ('Section: highway_status', SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:142).

Five different timestamp formats in one flow: Intl without seconds (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:20-26), Intl with seconds (SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:6-13), toLocaleString (submissionReviewerSupportModel.ts:27-37), 2-digit descriptor (utils/submissionLabel.ts:12-23), and raw ISO via String(value) (SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:24).

Duplicated stat-card markup: worklist summary cards (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:173-184) and photo-evidence summary cards (SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:97-102) share identical class strings and structure — extract one StatCard.
Duplicated error-banner markup with the same color-mix classes in SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:217, SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:86 and SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:384; none carry role=alert.

Two 'Preview unavailable in this browser' fallbacks with different content (SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:350-361 vs SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:135) and two presigned-URL strategies (cached resolver SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:24-75 vs raw download_url SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:133,143).

Two dropdown-menu implementations: the tile Open menu has role=menu, outside-click and Escape (SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:134-181,208-222) while the worklist '•••' menu has none of these (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:240).

MediaGlyph and MediaBadge compute the same type label with different precedence (glyph checks pdf first, badge checks photo/video first) — SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:105-122; attachmentTypeLabel is a third classifier (submissionReviewerSupportModel.ts:50-60) alongside attachmentMediaKind (submissionAttachmentModel.ts:81-91).

Dead/legacy code: SubmissionDetailPrimitives exports compatibility aliases S, R, Section (L68-79) of which only R is imported (pages/SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:16) and Section ignores its 'open' prop; attachmentActionLabel (submissionReviewerSupportModel.ts:62-67) is referenced only by its test; pages/SubmissionsPage.tsx:1 is a one-line re-export shim; SectionAttachmentsButton's 'disabled' prop is never passed (SubmissionSectionAttachmentsDialog.tsx:8; DetailPage 104,1258); the section dialog empty state is unreachable because the button hides at count 0 (SubmissionSectionAttachmentsDialog.tsx:9,53).

Photo evidence page overlaps the detail page: the detail page already fetches the same /photo-map (pages/SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:154,254), seeds thumbnails from it, and draws the map; the standalone page re-fetches and re-renders the same photos without the map (App.tsx:127-134).

Button styles: brand-filled primary only for 'Review' (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:239) and filter pills (SubmissionLibrary.tsx:50); red fill for Delete (SubmissionDeleteDialog.tsx:62); neutral 'rounded' + hover:brightness-95 for Grant/Revoke (SubmissionAccessSharing.tsx:67,95) vs 'rounded-md' + hover:bg-panel-soft elsewhere; tile buttons text-xs px-2 py-1 vs page buttons text-sm px-3 py-2; close affordances are a lucide X (SubmissionSectionAttachmentsDialog.tsx:48-50), a text '×' (SubmissionDeleteDialog.tsx:39), a text '•••' (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:240) and a text '←' (pages/SubmissionPhotoEvidencePage.tsx:52) next to lucide ArrowLeft (SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:326).

Accessibility: card and panel titles are styled divs rather than headings (SubmissionDetailPrimitives.tsx:53; SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:78) while the library uses h2 (SubmissionLibrary.tsx:33); role=tablist/tab without tabpanel or arrow keys (SubmissionLibrary.tsx:37-56); role=menu without keyboard navigation (SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:164-176); no aria-live/role=alert on any error or loading state; worklist table has no caption/aria-label (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:220).

Touch targets under 44px throughout: tile Open/Download (~24px, SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:158,273), filter pills (~26px, SubmissionLibrary.tsx:48), 'Open attachments' (~22px, SubmissionSectionAttachmentsDialog.tsx:15), '•••' and Review/Open (~32px, SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:239-240), Grant/Revoke (~28px, SubmissionAccessSharing.tsx:67,95).

Hover-only information: full file names and section labels (title attrs, SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:126,281,285), raw timestamps and creator ids (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:234-236), evidence heading tooltip (SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:119) are unreachable on touch devices; only the tile action overlay handles hover:none correctly (index.css:138-142).

Navigation: /submissions has no sidebar entry and no breadcrumbs anywhere in the flow; Assessments is highlighted for it (ui/AppShell.tsx:87) and RoleRoute uses it as the fallback (auth/RoleRoute.tsx:19); the only in-app links to the worklist are NotFoundPage and the invalid-id photo-evidence back link.

Internal ids are surfaced as user-facing data in every screen: '#id' on tiles (SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:287), 'Attachment #id' (SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:142), 'Actor user #id' (SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:52), 'User #id' (SubmissionsWorklistPage.tsx:234; SubmissionDeleteDialog.tsx:46), 'Corrected by user #id' (SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:161), raw event codes (SubmissionReviewerSupport.tsx:52) and MIME types (SubmissionPhotoEvidencePanel.tsx:148; SubmissionAttachmentTiles.tsx:355).
